iran.title: In Athens, Marco Rubio's civilisational hubris reaches a peak
iran.text: In Athens, Marco Rubio's civilisational hubris reaches a peak Submitted by Marco Carnelos on Thu, 10/22/2026 - 21:02 The US secretary of state holds up a flattering mirror to the West, ignoring centuries of catastrophic imperialism US Secretary of State Marco Rubio speaks in Athens, Greece, on 7 October 2026 (Mark Schiefelbein/AFP) Off On 7 October, US Secretary of State Marco Rubio delivered a remarkable speech in Athens. The event did not produce significant headlines - but it should have. Rubio’s statement deserves scrutiny, both because he could be a contender for the Republican nomination ahead of the 2028 presidential elections, and for the problematic nature of his comments (to say the least). Standing before the Parthenon, he delivered less a speech than a sermon on civilisational destiny. Rubio told his Athenian audience that the West owes the world its curiosity, its ambition, its “impatience with the notion of impossibility”. The setting was magnificent, and the rhetoric was built to match. Unfortunately, it was nothing more than an exercise in selective memory and civilisational vanity. Rubio’s central claim was that the ancient Greeks gave rise to traits that “would come to define the West”, setting it apart from “so many other cultures and civilisations where stability and subsistence were the highest ends of life”. This sentence deserves close attention. It essentially describes the builders of Cambodia’s Angkor temples, the astronomers of Samarkand, the engineers of the Inca road system, and the mathematicians of India ’s Kerala as people who aimed for subsistence. It ignores Ibn Battuta , who spent three decades crossing the known world, longer than Marco Polo’s journey. It overlooks the Polynesian navigators who settled the Pacific with no instruments.

north.title: Hijri's 'National Guard' militia closes Suweida-Damascus highway
north.text: Traffic on the key Suweida–Damascus road was completely halted on Saturday after the closure of the Umm al-Zaytun checkpoint, operated the self-styled 'National Guard' militia loyal to Druze spiritual leader Hikmat al-Hijri . Suweida's Media Directorate said that “outlaw groups at the Um al-Zaytun checkpoint are completely closing the Suweida–Damascus road and preventing citizens from travelling". This is not the first time that groups affiliated with the National Guard have closed the road, as they had previously shut the road at the Umm al-Zaytun checkpoint on several occasions, particularly during periods coinciding with school examinations, disrupting students’ travel and movement. The closure comes amid attempts by National Guard groups to infiltrate and carry out attacks in the western countryside of Suweida Governorate in recent days, without making any significant advances, according to the available information. On 8 October, factions affiliated with the National Guard took control of the village of Waqm in the western countryside of Suweida, in southern Syria, following an attack launched from the town of Areeqa. They withdrew from the village several hours after taking control of it. Speaking to The New Arab earlier this week, analysts said that the National Guard's activities are increasingly coinciding with the activities of Israeli forces occupying southern Syria, as well as moves by Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu to win over Palestinian Druze voters in the upcoming Israeli elections . Hijri, who leads the group, has frequently expressed support for Israeli involvement in Syria, saying earlier this year that the Druze are an "integral part of Israel". north.title: Protecting minorities: A test for Syria's new political order
north.text: Damascus - Almost two years on from the fall of Assad’s regime in 2024 , continued violence targeting Syria’s ethnic minorities is placing the country’s post-war recovery under strain as the government struggles to manage persistent sectarian tensions. Earlier this month, pro-government demonstrators gathered in Kurdish areas of Hasakeh and Raqqa, vandalising Kurdish symbols and calling for the government to take full control of the region. This comes amid the ongoing integration of the Kurdish-led SDF into the Syrian state. The unrest followed a series of mob attacks and acts of vandalism targeting Christian homes, vehicles and shops in Al-Suqaylabiyah , a predominantly Greek Orthodox town in Hama province. These are not isolated incidents. Post-Assad Syria has seen “several minority communities that have feared systemic discrimination and unfair treatment - particularly the Kurdish, Druze and Alawite communities,” Caroline Rose, a senior director at the Soufan Center, tells The New Arab . Al-Suqaylabiyah has already experienced a previous spate of mob violence over the past year, while Syria continues to witness sectarian killings on an almost daily basis. The country’s post-war recovery was also blighted by a series of massacres targeting Syria’s Alawite and Druze minorities in 2025. Syria’s decade-long civil war deepened sectarian hostility. Assad sought to frame the conflict as a sectarian war between Syria’s minority communities and Sunni “Islamists” and “terrorists”. As the revolution progressed, opposition to Assad became increasingly Islamist and sectarian in nature. north.title: Iran vows to block US warships from Gulf amid Trump threats
north.text: Iran said on Saturday that US military ships would never be allowed to enter the Gulf "under any circumstances" and that President Donald Trump would "take that dream to his grave". The remarks came amid mounting US and Israeli threats of renewed attacks on Iran, as US ambassador to Turkey Tom Barrack warned that Washington could "absolutely" strike Iran as soon as this weakened. "We will not allow US military ships in the Persian Gulf under any circumstances and at any time," said Iran's armed forces chief of staff Ali Abdollahi, according to Iranian state television. "The US president must dream of seeing the armed forces enter the Persian Gulf. He will take that dream to his grave." Iranian forces have restricted traffic through the Strait of Hormuz , a vital energy conduit and gateway to the Gulf, since the war with the United States broke out on 28 February. In retaliation, the United States has imposed a counterblockade on Iranian ports and ships. Tehran has required vessels to seek permission to transit, and repeatedly targeted ships attempting to pass through Hormuz via a southern route close to the Omani coast. According to the Guards, several tankers attempting to transit Hormuz through the route Tehran considers "illegal" were hit by mines in recent days. On Friday, the Guards said two supertankers carrying more than 4.5 million barrels of crude oil have been abandoned at sea after hitting mines in the strategic waterway. "Their engine rooms were disabled by an explosion and a fierce fire," the Guards said in a statement carried by their Sepah News website. In peacetime, around a fifth of the world's oil and gas passed through Hormuz. ukraine.title: Wreckage of foreign drone found in Latvia, investigation underway
ukraine.text: The wreckage of a drone that crashed on Latvian territory was found in the country's Alūksne district by the Latvian National Armed Forces on Saturday 24 October. Source: Latvian Armed Forces , as reported by European Pravda Details: The Latvian military reported that the unmanned aerial vehicle had likely entered Latvian airspace on 18 October. Following a report of a noise resembling an explosion, the National Armed Forces and State Police began searching for a possible crash site. The search was called off after two days because the initial information was insufficient to establish the circumstances of the incident. An investigation into the circumstances of the event is currently underway, and an internal review has been launched to assess the course of the incident and related circumstances. No civilians were injured in the incident, civilian infrastructure was not damaged, and no further threats have been identified. Background: On Sunday 18 October, the wreckage of a suspected drone that had violated the country's airspace was found in the village of Juodžionys, the Pasvalys district, Lithuania. Lithuania says the drone entered its airspace from Poland. Lithuanian Prime Minister Mindaugas Sinkevičius stated that the drone which flew into Lithuania on Sunday contained explosives . Heorhii Tykhyi, spokesman for Ukraine's Ministry of Foreign Affairs, stated that the drone incident in Lithuania was likely the result of Russian electronic warfare measures. He added that Ukraine expressed regret over the incident. Your support on Patreon helps us keep the news free and accessible.

ukraine.title: Ukraine’s military says Starlink satellite connection stable after recent restrictions
ukraine.text: Volodymyr Zelenskyy offers thanks to US allies for restoring system key to air defence and ‘frontline logistics’ Ukraine’s military has a “stable connection to Starlink”, the Ukrainian government has said, 10 days after its ability to use the satellite communications system was suddenly restricted . The Starlink satellite terminals, which are produced by Elon Musk’s SpaceX but managed by the US government, are a key component of Ukraine’s military operations. Sudden speed restrictions on the terminals, which capped operations at speeds of 160km/h (99mph), led to the failure of several Ukrainian combat missions earlier this month. Continue reading...

ukraine.title: Russian drone hits food shop in Nikopol district: four injured, including child
ukraine.text: A Russian drone struck a food shop in the Nikopol district in Dnipropetrovsk Oblast on Saturday 24 October, injuring three men and a 14-year-old boy. Source: National Police of Ukraine Quote: "Today, after 09:00, Russian forces launched an attack drone on a village in the Pokrovsk e hromada An administrative unit designating a village, several villages, or a town, and their adjacent territories . A local food shop, where people were present, has been hit" . Details: The police reported that a 14-year-old boy suffered severe injuries in the attack and has been taken to hospital in Dnipro. Three men aged between 45 and 58 were also injured and are in a moderate condition. They are receiving the necessary medical treatment. The strike damaged the shop and a metal fence. Police investigative teams are gathering information on the full consequences of the attack. Your support on Patreon helps us keep the news free and accessible.

ukraine.title: Zelensky: Ukraine awaits air defense interceptors, preparing meetings with partners
ukraine.text: Ukraine is continuing talks with the United States and European partners on resuming deliveries of interceptors to counter Russian ballistic missiles. It also expects diplomatic contacts to continue next week and humanitarian access to the town of Oleshky in the Kherson region to be unblocked.

ukraine.title: Drones attack chemical plant in Russia's Omsk, 2,500 km from Ukraine – OSINT
ukraine.text: Drones attacked the Omsky Kauchuk chemical plant in Russia on Saturday 24 October, causing a fire at the facility. Source: Exilenova+ , a Ukrainian OSINT community; Vitaly Khotsenko , Governor of Russia's Omsk Oblast; OSINT analyst Dnipro Osint ⟨Harbuz⟩ Details: OSINT analysts from the Exilenova+ community released a video of the strike. The drone attack sparked a large fire in the plant's industrial area. Khotsenko also confirmed the attack. OSINT analyst Dnipro Osint ⟨Harbuz⟩ noted that early reports indicate hits near two production units. The distance from Ukraine to the facility is approximately 2,500 km. "Early reports based on geolocation data indicate that hits were recorded near the D-3 (methyl tert-butyl ether production) and D-5 units," Dnipro Osint wrote. Locations at the Omsky Kauchuk plant that were hit in the latest strike Photos: Dnipro Osint (Harbuz) Background: Ukrainska Pravda previously reported that on the morning of 24 October, the defence forces struck the Togliattikauchuk plant in the city of Tolyatti, Samara Oblast, Russia. An explosion and a fire were recorded following the strike. On 23 October, the main production building of the Proton-Electrotex plant was also attacked in Oryol. The facility manufactures optoelectronic equipment and full-production-cycle devices. Your support on Patreon helps us keep the news free and accessible.

ukraine.title: One killed and two injured in Russian attack on business in Lozova, Kharkiv Oblast – photos
ukraine.text: A man was killed when Russian forces struck a business in the city of Lozova, Kharkiv Oblast, on Saturday 24 October. Source: Kharkiv Oblast Police Details: Two civilians aged 26 and 43 were injured in the attack. They have been taken to hospital to receive the necessary medical treatment. Police officers and other emergency services are working at the scene. Law enforcement officers are documenting the aftermath of the attack and collecting physical evidence. Investigators have launched a criminal investigation into the attack under Article 438 of the Criminal Code of Ukraine (war crimes). Support Ukrainska Pravda on Patreon to help us keep reporting!

yemen.text: US updates Gulf, Middle East travel advisories over threat of Houthi 'aggression' The United States updated travel advisories for countries across the Gulf and the wider Middle East, citing what it described as the threat of increased Iran-aligned Houthi "regional aggression", according to security alerts issued by US missions. yemen.text: Yemen's Houthis claim attack on Aden naval base, military camp Yemen's Houthis claimed an attack on Saturday on a naval base and a military camp in Aden, the interim seat of the internationally recognised government, after blasts were heard there. "Our armed forced targeted Saudi enemy concentrations at the so-called Al-Nasr camp and the naval base in Aden," Houthi military spokesman Yahya Saree said, adding that the sites were overseen by Saudi forces. Reporting by AFP

yemen.text: Houthis say Saudi strike kills five members of same family in Hodeida Yemen's Iran-backed Houthis on Saturday said a Saudi strike on Hodeida killed five members of the same family, as both sides carry out attacks. "Five people, the head of the family, two of his children and his two wives, have been martyred and his daughter wounded as a result of a Saudi enemy air strike on the home of citizen Abdulwahed al-Wasabi in the Al-Tuhayta district" of Hodeida, the Houthis' Al-Masirah TV channel reported. Reporting by AFP

yemen.title: Explosions heard in Yemen's city of Aden
yemen.text: Explosions heard in Yemen's city of Aden Explosions were heard on Saturday in Aden, a city in the south of the country that serves as the seat of the Saudi-backed Yemeni government, according to a police source and an AFP journalist. A police official in Aden told AFP that three explosions had been heard in the city, while an AFP correspondent also reported blasts.

Three killed in Saudi air strike on Sanaa, says Houthi-linked media
yemen.text: Three killed in Saudi air strike on Sanaa, says Houthi-linked media A Saudi airstrike on the Yemeni capital Sanaa killed three people on Saturday and wounded several others, according to Houthi-backed media. Al-Masirah station said "the Saudi enemy targeted a house in Asr", in the west of the capital. It added that the death toll was preliminary.

yemen.title: Iran vows to block US warships from Gulf amid Trump threats
yemen.text: Iran said on Saturday that US military ships would never be allowed to enter the Gulf "under any circumstances" and that President Donald Trump would "take that dream to his grave". The remarks came amid mounting US and Israeli threats of renewed attacks on Iran, as US ambassador to Turkey Tom Barrack warned that Washington could "absolutely" strike Iran as soon as this weakened. "We will not allow US military ships in the Persian Gulf under any circumstances and at any time," said Iran's armed forces chief of staff Ali Abdollahi, according to Iranian state television. "The US president must dream of seeing the armed forces enter the Persian Gulf. He will take that dream to his grave." Iranian forces have restricted traffic through the Strait of Hormuz , a vital energy conduit and gateway to the Gulf, since the war with the United States broke out on 28 February. In retaliation, the United States has imposed a counterblockade on Iranian ports and ships. Tehran has required vessels to seek permission to transit, and repeatedly targeted ships attempting to pass through Hormuz via a southern route close to the Omani coast. According to the Guards, several tankers attempting to transit Hormuz through the route Tehran considers "illegal" were hit by mines in recent days. On Friday, the Guards said two supertankers carrying more than 4.5 million barrels of crude oil have been abandoned at sea after hitting mines in the strategic waterway. "Their engine rooms were disabled by an explosion and a fierce fire," the Guards said in a statement carried by their Sepah News website. In peacetime, around a fifth of the world's oil and gas passed through Hormuz. yemen.title: Azmi Bishara: Trump has backed Netanyahu as his Iran war partner
yemen.text: Dr. Azmi Bishara has said US President Donald Trump is backing Benjamin Netanyahu in Israel's election because the two are partners in the war with Iran and share a wider regional agenda. Speaking to Al-Araby TV ahead of Israel's 27 October vote, the Arab thinker said Trump wanted Netanyahu to remain in power in order to "complete the mission" they had begun together. He argued that there was little fundamental difference between Israel's main governing and opposition blocs on Palestinian statehood or the country's broader regional posture. Bishara said much of the campaign instead revolved around security, the failures surrounding the 7 October 2023 attacks, military conscription and who could project greater military strength. Israel's election is currently too close to produce an obvious governing majority, with recent polling placing Netanyahu's bloc and Gadi Eisenkot's opposition coalition roughly level . Arab turnout 'critical' Bishara said Palestinian citizens of Israel nevertheless had a major stake in the election. He argued that growing efforts to delegitimise Arab political participation made turnout particularly important and described the vote as a decisive moment for Palestinian citizens. Bishara said higher participation could help block another government led by Netanyahu alongside far-right ministers Itamar Ben-Gvir and Bezalel Smotrich. He suggested Eisenkot's Yashar party could finish first but still struggle to form a government without support from Arab parties. That possibility has become central to the campaign, with Palestinian parties potentially holding the balance of power if neither bloc reaches the 61 seats needed for a Knesset majority. Bishara also said Washington favoured the idea of a unity government bringing Netanyahu and Eisenkot toge

yemen.title: Pakistan ratifies Mecca pact as Saudi Arabia faces attacks and Israel holds military drills
yemen.text: Pakistan ratifies Mecca pact as Saudi Arabia faces attacks and Israel holds military drills Submitted by MEE staff on Sat, 10/24/2026 - 10:25 Saudi authorities have lifted recent security alerts, while Washington signals the possibility of military action against Tehran A man takes a picture of a billboard featuring Pakistan's Army Chief General Syed Asim Munir (C), Naval Chief Admiral Naveed Ashraf (R) and Air Chief Marshal Zaheer Ahmed Babar Sidhu in Peshawar, 15 May 2025 (Abdul Majeed/AFP) Off Pakistan on Friday announced that it has ratified a joint defence pact with Turkey and Saudi Arabia as the kingdom faces renewed security threats and is looking for allies to help it against Yemen's Houthis. Pakistan’s Foreign Office spokesperson, Sajjad Haider Khan, said that Islamabad and Riyadh have completed their ratification procedures for the Mecca Joint Defence Agreement, signed by the three countries on 7 August. “Matters related to the agreement, its ratification, and operationalisation remain under discussion by the three parties,” Khan said, according to a transcript published by Pakistan’s Foreign Office. Turkey is still completing its domestic approval process as the agreement has not yet completed ratification by all three signatories. The pact was signed in Mecca by Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan, Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif and Saudi Arabia's Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman . It provides for collective defence in the event of an external armed attack against any of the three countries, with the nature and level of assistance to be determined according to the circumstances.
